testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

unverified.claim: The reworded step-7 clause "refuses … a second, different Routing for that name" is one of the ticket's acceptance-criterion sites, but no test pins it: reverting it to the old literal `impl-<N>` passes every test that reads pull.md's step 7.
unverified.evidence: In the copy I ran `perl -0pi -e 's/Routing for that name;/Routing for \`impl-<N>\`;/' pull.md` and then `node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/render-before-dispatch-prose.test.mjs tests/within-run-pair-prose.test.mjs tests/run-team-pull-prose.test.mjs`, which printed `# fail 0` (mutant M3 survived). The other five reverts were all caught: row example `# fail 2`, behind-issue rewrite `# fail 1`, 'verbatim under' `# fail 1`, 'marks live' `# fail 2`, render/record order swap `# fail 2`. A grep of snapshot tests/ for `second,? different|Routing for|not a Routing|different Routing` finds only ledger.test.mjs:3977 (behaviour) and ledger-grammar/ledger-rotate code tests. No prose pin exists, and the moved-text fixture's step-7 slice ends at 'have just claimed. Router' without that sentence. The full suite was not run against this mutant.
unverified.suggested_fix: In within-run-pair-prose.test.mjs's step-7 test, add an assertion such as `assert.match(slice, /second,\s+different\s+Routing\s+for\s+that\s+name/, …)` next to the new `<member>` pin.

unverified.claim: Step 7 and the record-the-dispatch paragraph define `<member>` as "the name the Pull printed", but pull.mjs prints the member name only in the final `DISPATCH {"name",…}` line, after row, render and dispatch have run. A reader stepping through step 7 has seen no printed name yet; the naming rule at pull.md:694 says the member is "named", not printed, before the claim.
unverified.evidence: Reasoned, not executed. Grep of the snapshot's plugin/scripts/pull.mjs for `DISPATCH|st.member` shows the name is set at :965 (`st.member = member`), used at :1012/:1024/:1035, and printed only at :1056 (`DISPATCH ${JSON.stringify(this.st.dispatch)}`, name: st.member at :1044). The ticket's Agent Brief prescribes 'the name the Pull printed' wording, so the PR follows the ticket.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optional: phrase it as the member the Pull named (the `name` its `DISPATCH` line prints), matching pull.md:694-704. Not required by the ticket.
